mainEntity.name: برای API از استاندارد خاصی استفاده می‌کنید؟

acceptedAnswer.text: اگر API شما مشخصات OpenAPI دارد یا می‌تواند داشته باشد، مرجع را از روی آن می‌سازیم تا با کد هم‌گام بماند.

mainEntity.name: Do you use a standard for API docs?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your API has, or can have, an OpenAPI specification, we build the reference from it so it stays in step with the code.

mainEntity.name: دفتر تصمیم‌ها چه فرقی با صورت‌جلسه دارد؟

acceptedAnswer.text: صورت‌جلسه می‌گوید چه گفته شد. دفتر تصمیم‌ها می‌گوید چه تصمیمی گرفته شد، چرا، و کدام گزینه‌ها رد شد.

mainEntity.name: How is a decision log different from meeting minutes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minutes record what was said. A decision log records what was decided, why, and which options were rejected.

blocks.html: Documents the next maintainer can use, with a named audience, format, and update rule.

items: When technical knowledge and key decisions live in one person's head, that person leaving stops the work. A document that exists but has no one responsible for updating it stops being reliable after a few changes.
Teams with a product or API that customers or outside developers must use without asking you.
Businesses moving a project from one team or contractor to another.
Teams that want to know why a technical decision was made, not only what was decided.
If you want a document that sits in a folder and nobody reads.
If access to the system, the code, or the people who know it is not possible. Documentation without a source is guesswork.
If you need legal text (contracts, terms of use, a formal privacy policy); that is a lawyer's job.
Audit. Input: existing documents, system access, and conversations with key people. Output: a list of what exists, what is missing, and what is wrong. Owner: dadmor.
Structure. Input: the audit. Output: a document list with audience, format, update rule and owner for each. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
Write. Input: approved structure and access to sources. Output: the documents, reviewed by one person on your team. Owner: dadmor; technical review: you.
Handover. Input: approved documents. Output: documents in their final location, with a session showing how to keep them updated. Owner: dadmor.
What changes the size of the work: number of documents, number of API endpoints, bilingual output, and how available the sources (code, people) are.
What you supply: system and code access, key people's time, and one technical reviewer.
What delays projects: a key person with no time to talk, and a system that changes while it is being documented.
A separate fixed proposal for each phase. The audit can be ordered on its own.

blocks.html: A band is the rough size of the work, not a price and not a duration. A fixed price is set only after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.
The band is a starting estimate; the scoping conversation may move it.

items: A document stays correct only while its update rule is followed. After handover, that is the job of the owner named in the structure.
We do not write legal text.
We publish a sample of your documents only with your permission, and redacted.
